recipes.name: Crock Pot Cheesy Mushroom Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Place the chicken breasts into a slow cooker. Whisk the cream of chicken soup, cream of mushroom soup, sherry, garlic, celery flakes, and paprika in a mixing bowl. Stir in the Parmesan cheese and mushroom pieces; pour over the chicken.
Cook on Low for 8 hours until the chicken is tender, and the sauce has reduced slightly.

raw_recipe.headline: Crock Pot Cheesy Mushroom Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breasts are slow cooked in sherry, cream of chicken, and cream of mushroom soup in this tasty dish that goes well over egg noodles or rice.

review.reviewBody: White wine or chicken broth can be used in place of the cooking sherry. (Might want to use low-salt or homemade chicken stock, as the cream-of soups can be a bit salty.) To stretch this further, add a sliced onion and another can of mushrooms. This is a very cost-effective recipe I make in the crockpot often, varying the ingredients I have in my pantry. Chicken can be bought marked down and most of the ingredients called for can be bought at a discount grocery store or the dollar store. It's great for energy conservation as the crockpot costs less to power than your stove. I like it over mashed potatoes, kids like it on rice or over egg noodles.
My family loved this! I used 2 cans of cream of mushroom. It was a little soupy, but I made it with mashed potatoes, so I had instant gravy. YUM I baked it in the oven @400 for 45 minutes
I will definately make this again. Tasty, inexpensive, and easy! I made it without celery flakes and I used fresh mushrooms rather than canned. I also added an sliced onion. Served over egg noodles.

I used white wine instead of the sherry as other reviews suggested (more than 1/2 a cup). I also used fresh shredded parm cheese, not the grated kind. I added Rosemary, a little bit of rubbed sage, ground pepper, one can of cream of mushroom soup and one can of cream of celery soup, paprika, parsley flakes and a little bit of celery seed (didn't have celery flakes) and a good amount of minced garlic (way more than one teaspoon). I use whatever I have on hand to make this and my family loves it. The white wine adds such a nice flavor that I actually don't like to make it unless I have some dry white white. I used Sutter Home Chardonnay this time. I also added a can of mushrooms. I used frozen chicken breasts and cook on high for 4-5 hours. If I have fresh chicken, I cook on low for 7-8 hours. I like this over rice or egg noodles. Awesome, satisfying comfort food! Make it your way...enjoy!

After reading the reviews, I too made some changes and I was so pleased with the results! I doubled the soup so I had 2 cream of chicken and 2 cream of mushroom soups. The night before, I sauteed two 8 ounce packages of fresh mushrooms with two fresh cloves minced along with half of a large yellow onion finely chopped. So in the morning, I placed 8 chicken breasts, with all of the ingredients as described except I too couldn't find celery flakes, so I used parsley flakes. I did use the cooking sherry and it was delicious! Thank you so much!

This was great and easy! I used what was in my cabinets, so I substituted fresh baby bella mushrooms, parsley flakes and cooking white wine instead of the canned mushrooms, celery flakes and cooking sherry. I did cook it on low for 7 hours and kept it warm for 2-3 and the chicken was perfect.

Great! I tweaked a bit but followed the main steps. This is an excellent recipe! Used white wine vs. sherry, added 3 fresh cloves garlic and a med. onion (sautéed in garlic with garlic canola oil), 2 cans mushrooms and used rosemary. For the Parmesan, I used 1/4 c pecorino and 1/4 c shredded asiago. Then I topped the chicken with mozzarella 1/2 hr before we ate. Served over brown rice with Brussel sprouts

Husband loved this! Halved the recipe because there is just two of us. Chicken was moist and sauce was very tasty. I served over store bought noodles. Since there was less chicken it was done in less time. Very good!

This was an easy one... and very tasty... layered chicken legs cut in half.. saute celery, onions, and fresh garlic... put 1/2 in bottom.... 1/2 chicken... half soups then did it again... Then put Yukon Gold potates and fresh carrots on top... salt and pepper and turkey spice from Epicure .. cooked on high for 4 hrs...

BTW, celery flakes are sold thru Amazon. I added a cup of celery, used celery soup, added a tsp. of chopped garlic, a pkg of Italian dressing, When almost done add a block of cream cheese, cook for about 15 min or when it is softened it is ready to put over rice or noodles. Tonight I am putting it over sweet potatoes!

Full flavor Super simple fall comfort food. I made this pretty much as written. I used fresh mushrooms instead of canned, added extra garlic and celery stick, served over mashed potatoes. Will definitely make again!
I made this recipe and it was absolutely delicious. I plan on making it again and again. Goes well with rice or maybe even some pasta. Leftovers can be good in a pot pit.

I also used a can of cream of celery with the cream of chicken and cream of mushroom. I did not use mushrooms (which I absolutely love), but my children do not like mushrooms. I also added 'Vegeta' seasoning compared to the last time I made this for more flavor. Also used great on egg noodles.

I loved this! Chicken was so tender and the sauce was flavorful. I didn’t have cream of chicken soup so I used 2 cans of cream of mushroom soup. I only had an 8 oz can of mushrooms and that seemed fine. I will definitely make this again.
Quite good! I made with breasts and thighs and I feel way too much soup was called for. Next time I would use half can of each soup for 4 chicken pieces.

The chicken came out tender, but the sauce was reduced pretty much. That was because I didn't make a whole recipe. I think if anyone is going to cook a half or a third of a recipe, reduce the time too.
Just ok. Needs some additional spices for flavor. Chicken was super moist, though. very easy to make.
We did not care for this at all.

Like other recipes, I have had this in my recipe box for some time. So I finally made it and it was terrific. I made a few slight changes based on necessity. I had no celery flakes so I used parsley. That was fine. I only had a cut up chicken so I used that. I prefer it. The bones and the skin gave lots of flavor. and the skin just peeled away. Finally, I used fresh mushrooms even though I had the canned ones. I way prefer them and they gave this recipe a wonderful depth of flavor. I will be making this again.
Very dry, little flavor
